intro: Kabaddi is a contact team sport from the Indian subcontinent that mixes tag and wrestling. One player — the raider — crosses into the opponents' half, tries to touch defenders and get back across the midline, while the defenders try to stop the raider from returning. Traditionally raiders chant 'kabaddi, kabaddi' on a single breath; modern professional leagues use a raid timer instead. This entry summarises standard (court) kabaddi as played internationally and in professional leagues.
inThirtySeconds: Teams take turns sending a raider into the opponents' half.
The raider scores a point for every defender touched — if they make it back across the midline.
Defenders score by stopping the raider from getting back (a tackle).
Players who are 'out' leave the court and come back when their team scores.
objective: Score more points than the opponent through successful raids, tackles and all-outs.

facts.players: 7 per team on court, with substitutes

scoring.label: Touch point
scoring.detail: For each defender the raider touches before returning safely.

scoring.label: Bonus point
scoring.detail: Raider crosses the bonus line with a foot while enough defenders are on court.

scoring.label: Tackle point
scoring.detail: Defenders stop the raider from returning.

scoring.label: All out
scoring.detail: Bonus for eliminating the entire opposing team.

bodies.name: Pro Kabaddi League
bodies.scope: Professional league in India with its own playing rules

rules.title: Raiding
rules.summary: The raider crosses the midline into the opponents' half, tries to touch one or more defenders, and must return across the midline to score.
rules.body: Traditionally the raider must keep chanting 'kabaddi' in one breath for the whole raid ('cant'); losing the cant gets the raider out. Professional leagues instead give the raider 30 seconds to complete the raid. Each team sends raiders alternately.
rules.example: A raider touches two defenders with a toe-touch and dives back over the midline: two points, and both defenders are out.

rules.title: Baulk line and bonus line
rules.summary: The raider must cross the baulk line in the opponents' half for the raid to count; crossing the further bonus line can earn a bonus point.
rules.body: If the raider returns without crossing the baulk line or touching a defender, the raid is unsuccessful. The bonus point only applies when a minimum number of defenders (usually six) are on court.

rules.title: Do-or-die raid
rules.summary: In professional leagues, after two consecutive empty raids the team's third raid must score — or the raider is out.
rules.body: This rule stops teams playing safe with empty raids and creates high-pressure moments.

rules.title: The tackle
rules.summary: Defenders score a point if they hold the raider and stop them returning to their half.
rules.body: Defenders may hold the raider by the torso and limbs but not by the hair or clothing, and may not use dangerous holds such as gripping the throat. Successful tackles with three or fewer defenders on court earn an extra 'super tackle' point.

rules.title: Out and revival
rules.summary: Players who are out leave the court; each point scored by their team brings one teammate back, in the order they went out.
rules.body: If a team loses all its players, the opponents score an 'all out' bonus and the whole team returns. This revival system means the number of players on court changes constantly.

rules.title: Boundaries and the lobby
rules.summary: Players who step out of bounds are out; the side 'lobby' strips only become part of the court once contact is made during a raid.
rules.body: A defender who pushes the raider out of bounds without a legal tackle may give the raider the point.

fouls.name: Losing the cant / raid time
fouls.description: Raider stops chanting or exceeds the raid timer.

fouls.name: Stepping out of bounds
fouls.description: Leaving the playing area without contact having been made.

fouls.name: Illegal hold
fouls.description: Holding by the hair, kit or throat.
fouls.consequence: Point to the raider, possible card

flow.title: Toss
flow.description: The winner chooses court side or first raid.

flow.title: Alternating raids
flow.description: Teams send raiders one after another.

flow.title: Final raids
flow.description: Tactical substitutions and do-or-die moments decide close matches.

positions.name: Raider
positions.role: Attacker who enters the opponents' half.

positions.name: Corner defenders
positions.role: Specialists at the ends of the defensive chain.

positions.name: All-rounder
positions.role: Player who both raids and defends.

field.name: Court
field.dimensions: About 13 m × 10 m for men (smaller for women and juniors)
notes: Baulk line and bonus line in each half

glossary.definition: The continuous chant of 'kabaddi' during a raid.
A tackle made when three or fewer defenders remain.
Eliminating every player on the opposing team.
A quick extended-leg touch on a defender.

funFacts: Kabaddi has been played at the Asian Games since 1990.
The Pro Kabaddi League, launched in 2014, turned the sport into a major television event in India.
